statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk stays low and well below the block threshold after an orderly two-sided 25 August session, while Stress is elevated on a fresh post-close software guidance disappointment and the stacked 26 August releases that precede the NVIDIA report.
recommendation: The 25 August cash session closed with NQ futures settling 29,287.50, up 0.62%, mid-range inside a 268-point band after the intraday pullback to 29,157.25 was absorbed rather than extended. VIX finished at 14.89, both key Treasury yields eased and WTI fell 4.6% as U.S.-Iran tension receded, which describes functioning rather than failing mean reversion, so the mapped state remains EA_ON. Intuit's below-consensus fiscal 2027 guidance sent its shares about 9% lower post-market and will be priced at the 22:00Z Globex reopen; at that index weight it is treated as a Stress input. A narrow danger window is marked from the 26 August 12:30Z PCE, GDP and durable-goods stack through 15:00Z, where conditional forecast Tail reaches the watch band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: Nasdaq-100 ends an orderly two-sided session with volatility, yields and crude all lower, as Intuit's guidance cut hands the 22:00Z reopen its first test before Wednesday's PCE, GDP and NVIDIA stack
body: NQ futures settled 29,287.50 on 25 August, up 181.75 points or 0.62%, inside a 29,157.25-29,425.75 range roughly 268 points wide, finishing about 130 points above the low and 138 below the high. The structurally decisive observation is that the intraday pullback was absorbed and reversed rather than failing: the tape kept an upward bias while staying clearly two-sided, and mean reversion worked throughout the session. U.S. cash confirms the tone without any sign of one-way structure, with the S&P 500 up 0.32% to 7,677.28, the Nasdaq Composite up 0.66% to 26,151.30, the Dow up 0.30% to 53,577.40 and QQQ up 0.62% to 710.72. Cross-assets support rather than amplify that read. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.0% with a 14.77-15.95 range, the 10-year yield eased about seven basis points to 4.63% and the 2-year sits near 4.19%, while WTI fell 4.59% to 81.11 and Brent 5.60% to 87.01 after investors judged the latest U.S. sanctions on Iran to be economic pressure rather than a supply shock, with Pakistan's army chief visiting Tehran on a diplomatic track. Leadership was narrow but constructive: the semiconductor group was firm with AMD up 4.91%, Micron 2.48%, NVIDIA 2.19% and six of seven tracked names higher, NVIDIA snapping a seven-day losing streak, while the megacap group split evenly four to four as Apple, Alphabet, Amazon and Broadcom finished lower. That split is a conviction-reducing rather than a Tail-amplifying condition. The new development since the prior assessment is corporate rather than macro: Intuit reported fiscal Q4 revenue of 4.4 billion dollars and non-GAAP EPS of 4.03, both ahead of consensus, but set fiscal 2027 non-GAAP EPS guidance of 22.88 to 23.12 dollars against a materially higher consensus, and its shares traded about 9% lower post-market near 21:00Z. At Intuit's index weight this is a single-name and enterprise-software read-across issue rather than an index-level one-way mechanism, so it is scored through Stress. Today's macro was soft without being disorderly: Conference Board consumer confidence printed 89.4 against 90.2 expected, the weakest since January, and July new home sales fell 10.5% month over month to 607,000. Canada's retaliatory tariffs on roughly 20 billion dollars of U.S. goods, at rates of 15%, 25% and 50% effective 8 September, remain a live policy thread that has not produced index-level one-way structure. Tail is set at 11: there is no persistent directional efficiency, no sequence of failed retracements and no cluster of aligned amplifiers, the cash close removes the intraday continuation channel, and CME equity-index futures are inside the 21:00-22:00Z maintenance break so no price path is forming at the assessment cutoff. Stress is 47, two points above the prior reading, because the Intuit guidance cut adds a genuine reopen repricing to an already heavy 26 August stack that combines the July PCE and core PCE price indices, the second Q2 GDP estimate, advance durable goods and personal income and outlays at 12:30Z with the NVIDIA report at 20:20Z. Confidence is 88: verified futures settlement and day range, cash index closes, VIX, both key yields, crude in both benchmarks, breadth, megacap and semiconductor tone, verified corporate results, the verified event calendar with consensus figures, and fresh shared delayed cross-asset context were all available and mutually consistent.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours the assessment never left the low-to-watch Tail band. Tail sat between 7 and 12 through the 24 August U.S. evening and the Asian session under normal and mixed modes, then built steadily from 04:00Z on 25 August as a trend-up bias developed, reaching 15 to 17 by the European morning. Between 09:00Z and 13:00Z the reading held the 20-21 watch band across the European session, the U.S. pre-market and the first cash hour, the only stretch of the window mapped to yellow. From 14:00Z the mode reverted to mixed as the U.S. session produced two-way trade rather than continuation, and Tail unwound steadily to 12 by 18:00Z before easing to 11 into the cash close. Stress stayed in the elevated 42-51 band throughout and Confidence held between 84 and 88, so the de-escalation reflects observed structure rather than thinning evidence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours divide into four phases. The first is the 21:00-22:00Z CME maintenance break, in which no price path forms, followed by the 22:00Z Globex reopen where Intuit's guidance cut is priced for the first time; conditional Tail is 11 to 12 there, covering thin-liquidity slippage rather than an assumed direction. The second phase is the overnight Asian and early European stretch, which carries no scheduled U.S. release and where conditional Tail eases to its low point of 10 on an assumed contained range. The third phase is the European morning and U.S. pre-market, where conditional Tail drifts from 13 to 17 as positioning into the release stack builds and ranges are assumed to compress rather than trend. The fourth is the 26 August data stack: conditional Tail steps into the watch band at 23 for the 12:00Z hour containing the 12:30Z PCE, GDP, durable-goods and personal-income releases, peaks at 24 for the 13:00Z hour where post-release discovery meets the U.S. cash open, then eases to 21 and back below the watch band from 15:00Z as the repricing is assumed to be absorbed. Conditional Tail then re-enters the watch band at 20 for the final slot, because NVIDIA reports at 20:20Z into thin post-close liquidity. Stress follows a similar arc and peaks at 64. Confidence declines from 88 to 72 across the window, which is the normal decay of forecast evidence quality with distance rather than a deterioration in current evidence.
